sources.title: The Syntax of the Dialect of Bari (PhD dissertation)
sources.author: Luigi Andriani
sources.reliability_notes: Fieldwork-based morphosyntax of urban Barese: SVO/null subjects, impersonal zə, postnominal adjectives and possessives, enclitic kinship possessives, demonstratives (cùssə/cùddə, stu/sta/sti), BE/HAVE paradigms, person-split auxiliary selection (so'/sì/à/sìmə/sìtə/ònnə), present perfect vs preterite, STAND/GO periphrases with inflected 2sg/3sg, stà/scì paradigms, prohibitive with sì+gerund. Only facts and short forms are cited; no passages copied.

sources.title: Note linguistiche sul cinema di Leonardo Pieraccioni (in Scritti per Nicoletta Maraschio, Accademia della Crusca, 2018)

sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.reliability_notes: Short lead definitions only: ammuina = confusione; scugnizzo = monello di strada napoletano; guappo; 'nciucio/'nciucià = pettegolezzo/spettegolare; pucchiacca = Neapolitan vulgar term for vulva (article Fica). Other URLs: https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scugnizzo, https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guappo, https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inciucio, https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fica

sources.title: La frutta realistica ci ha fatto la uallera, video virale
sources.reliability_notes: Contemporary press attestation of the spelling 'uallera' and of the phrase 'ci ha fatto la uallera' glossed as 'ci ha stufato oltre ogni immaginazione'.

sources.title: Glossary of Neapolitan: the most used and known words in Naples and beyond
sources.reliability_notes: Tourism glossary; used only as corroboration for colloquial items (alluccare, arronzare, arteteca, appiccecarse, ammuccarse, cazzimma, chiattillo, 'nzallanuto, 'nziria, 'nzisto, sarchiapone, scuorno, vrenzola, vattere, lloco).

sources.title: Vocabolario napolitano-italiano tascabile ... preceduto da brevi osservazioni grammaticali
sources.author: Pietro Paolo Volpe
sources.publisher: Napoli; digitized by Google, hosted on Internet Archive
sources.reliability_notes: Only the introductory 'Brevi osservazioni grammaticali' were used (sound correspondences b>v, d>r, nd>nn, pl>chi, bi>j, fi>sci, glide insertion pajese/voje; article and plural doubling). OCR very noisy.

sources.title: Modi di dire napoletani
sources.author: Wikiquote contributors
sources.reliability_notes: Idioms with explanations and references to printed works (Apicella 'Il frasario napoletano', 'Manuale di napoletanità', contemporary novels). Key: 'Me staje abbuffanno 'a guallera' (annoy to death) and hyperbolic variants ''a guallara a pezzaiuola', 'sfaccimma', 'cazzimma', 'chiaveca'. Meanings rewritten.

sources.title: Proverbi napoletani
sources.author: Wikiquote contributors
sources.reliability_notes: Large collection, many items cite printed sources (e.g. 'I Proverbi di Napoli'). Spelling is not uniform and a few items are from other Campanian varieties (u/i articles): only items in city-Neapolitan form were adopted. Meanings rewritten in our own words.

sources.title: Wiktionary Neapolitan and Italian entries (machine-readable extract by kaikki.org)
sources.author: Wiktionary contributors; extraction by Tatu Ylonen (wiktextract)
sources.reliability_notes: Neapolitan coverage is thin and mixes regional forms; used only for corroboration: cazzimma (borrowed into Italian from Neapolitan, from cazzo + -imma; cynical opportunism / gratuitous malice), ricchione (vulgar derogatory slur), guaglione, ajere, dimane, accussì, chiagnere.

sources.title: Un amminchiato si fissa, il crastu è un furbo: in viaggio tra i modi di dire in Sicilia
sources.reliability_notes: Word list (amminchiatu, scantusu, vastasu, fitusu, tintu, lagnusu) and sayings; the article itself says usage varies by place, so items are treated as general Sicilian. Read through a tool summary.

sources.title: Chiù longa è a pinsata, chiù grossa è a minchiata: come nasce un modo di dire siciliano
sources.reliability_notes: Humorous column; documents the saying and the addumari/astutari 'turn on/off' pair. Read through a tool summary.

sources.title: C'è chi si arrimina e chi è una camurria: alcune parole siciliane (quasi) intraducibili
sources.reliability_notes: Ten Sicilian words glossed by a Palermo outlet (arriminarsi, annacarsi, azzizzari, camurria, ammatula, abbuttato, mizzica, strafalaru); not Palermo-exclusive.

sources.title: Insostituibile nel bene e nel male: elogio di una termine che racconta la storia, minchia
sources.reliability_notes: Opinion piece in a Palermo outlet (2018); documents the many uses of minchia and quotes the phrase 'teste di minchia'.

sources.title: In Sicilia con una parola puoi dire una cosa e il contrario: storia di un malaminnitta
sources.reliability_notes: First-person column written partly in Palermitano (ra, picca, ni fazzu minnitta, sminnò, pigghiata); cites Traina's dictionary for minnitta.

sources.title: Cuinnutu, vaistunatu e pure attassato: se ti ci rivedi in Sicilia sei un mischino
sources.reliability_notes: Column with Palermo-area speech samples (Ma chi minchia cunti?, si na minchia sicca, mischinu as filler); etymology claims (Arabic miskin) are the author's and are not repeated as fact.

sources.title: Il siciliano è una babele: una spiegazione alla sanfasò di alcune famose frasi di uso comune
sources.reliability_notes: Explains Palermo phrases (muriu u cani, finìu a cachi, chi nicchi e nacchi, sanfasò, fetenzia, malaminchiata). Read through a tool summary of the page, not line by line.

sources.title: Da tabù a poliedrico mito pop: il suca nasce, cresce e prospera, e non solo in Sicilia
sources.reliability_notes: Feature on the graffiti and social meanings of suca in Palermo, with an interview of a semiotics graduate.

sources.title: Proposta di normalizzazione ortografica comune della lingua siciliana, I edizione 2017
sources.reliability_notes: Orthography proposal; the Palermitano remarks are brief asides (descending diphthong [jɛ] for <e>, loss of intervocalic g: agustu read as austu) but come from a language-planning body.

sources.title: Dialetto palermitano (Wikipedia in italiano)
sources.reliability_notes: Stub article flagged by Wikipedia itself for missing citations; used only for the diphthongization of stressed vowels (bìeddu, cacùocciulu) and the sample text of UDHR art. 1 in Palermitano.

sources.title: A trip in Sicily? The Palermitan words every Tourist needs to know
sources.author: Saverio Schirò
sources.reliability_notes: Tourist-oriented list by an editor; useful for market vocabulary (abbanniari, pattiari, tastari) and everyday interjections as used in Palermo.

sources.title: Detti, proverbi e... scongiuri palermitani
sources.reliability_notes: Unsigned editorial page; spellings are in Palermo orthography (ru, ra, uocchi, duormi, buonu, malutiempu) and several items are explicitly tied to Palermo (cassaro, festino, vara di San Domenico). Printed typos noted in entries.

sources.title: Asini e scecchi. Una lettura degli usi fraseologici e paremiologici asinini in italiano e siciliano
sources.author: Ivana Vermiglio
sources.reliability_notes: Peer-reviewed paper (Università di Palermo, Lingue e Linguaggi 61, 2024) on Sicilian donkey phraseology; forms come from several Sicilian areas, not only Palermo.

sources.title: Sonetti romaneschi (ed. Morandi), transcribed on Wikisource: Li soprani der monno vecchio (1832), Er caffettiere fisolofo (1833), Er giorno der giudizzio (1831)
sources.author: Giuseppe Gioachino Belli
sources.license: Public domain text; Wikisource transcription CC BY-SA
sources.reliability_notes: Primary literary source for historical Romanesco. Also read: Er caffettiere fisolofo (Pagina:Sonetti romaneschi II.djvu/395), Er giorno der giudizzio (Pagina:Sonetti romaneschi I.djvu/533).

sources.title: «E fra le dita, sola / frìccica una parola». Un friccico di romanesco nell'italiano contemporaneo
sources.author: Kevin De Vecchis
sources.publisher: Edizioni Università per Stranieri di Siena
sources.reliability_notes: Study of frìccico / friccicà(re) / friccicore.

sources.title: Romanesco: The Voice of Rome (Italian grammar, regional section)
sources.reliability_notes: Learner page; corroborates 1pl forms (stamo, annamo, famo, avemo), regà, 'na cifra, c'ho.

sources.title: Romanesco dialect
sources.reliability_notes: History (Tuscanization, Belli, Trilussa), modern pronunciation features, classical vs modern comparison table (dovamo, ce l'avamo, inguattà, nja faccio).

sources.title: Romanesco: 25 Cool Roman Dialect Words You Should Use in Rome
sources.author: Michele Frolla
sources.reliability_notes: Popular travel blog; used only for contemporary colloquialisms, corroborated where possible.

sources.title: Dialetto romanesco
sources.reliability_notes: Phonology (rhotacism, -nd->-nn-, Lex Porena), articles, sections on vulgar terminology, religion-related expressions, proverbs and money slang. Facts rephrased.

sources.title: Grammatica del romanesco
sources.reliability_notes: Paradigms of articles, pronouns, possessives, demonstratives and irregular verbs. The page itself flags that it relies on one source and lacks some citations; cross-checked against Belli, Zanazzo, VRC and Wiktionary where possible.

sources.title: Wikizionario: entries sola, sbroccare, cazzaro, zozzo, sticazzi, paraculo, mignotta, fregnone, abbiocco, sgamare, rosicare
sources.reliability_notes: Used to corroborate regional/Roman labels of colloquial and vulgar items.

sources.title: Il confine fluido dell'etimologia romanesca e la diacronia del lessico capitolino (in «'E parole de Roma», De Gruyter 2020), post-print
sources.author: Michele Loporcaro
sources.reliability_notes: Etymology and semantic history of Roman words that entered Italian (racchia, mignotta, inguattare, bacarozzo, pupo, ciumaca, cacchio...). Notes the vulgar skew of the surviving distinctive lexicon.

sources.title: La lettera «D» del «Vocabolario del romanesco contemporaneo» (Studi di lessicografia italiana XXXVIII, 2021, pp. 347-395), post-print
sources.author: Paolo D'Achille, Claudio Giovanardi, Vincenzo Faraoni, Michele Loporcaro
sources.linguistic_area: Romanesco (Rome), contemporary dialect and regional Italian
sources.reliability_notes: Scholarly dictionary of contemporary Romanesco (Roma Tre / Zurich). Entries for daje, de, der/dar, Lex Porena forms, many idioms and proverbs.
sources.relevant_sections: §§1-2 criteria; lemmario: dàje1/dàje2, dàcce, dàlla, dassela, de, dea/dee/dii/doo, diavolo, debbito, dritto, domani, duro, devasto, deçino, delirio

sources.title: Wiktionary: Category:Romanesco Italian and individual entries (daje, aridaje, anvedi, ahó, ammazza, ammappa, mo, pischello, coatto, mortacci, me cojoni, sticazzi, etc.)
sources.reliability_notes: Category of ~600 terms (many medieval/archaic) plus entries read individually as raw wikitext. Only entries actually read are cited; meanings rephrased.

sources.title: Proverbi romaneschi
sources.author: Giggi Zanazzo
sources.reliability_notes: First systematic collection of Roman proverbs, transcribed from oral use; Belli-style spelling with written syntactic doubling (ppiù, bbene). Read via the archive.org OCR text; OCR errors corrected by comparison with context. A few items are marked by Zanazzo as from Albano Laziale.
sources.relevant_sections: Consiglio; Errore; Esperienza; Ozio-Lavoro; Pazienza; Parlare-Tacere; Prudenza; Riflessione-Tempo; Risolutezza; Sapere; Schiettezza; Scherzi

sources.title: Dizionario leccese-italiano (online edition)
sources.author: Antonio Garrisi
sources.license: All rights reserved (author's work published online)
sources.reliability_notes: Large single-author dictionary of the Lecce/Cavallino variety with full verb paradigms, usage examples, about 1,200 proverbs and an explicit orthographic note on the cacuminal sound (written δδ) and the simple/long sh sounds (sç/sc). It is not peer-reviewed, but it is the most detailed open source for the city variety and agrees with the academic descriptions. The front matter was read in full. All letter pages (A-Z) were downloaded and searched entry by entry for the items used. Definitions were rewritten in our own words, not copied.
sources.relevant_sections: Prefazione/Avvertenze (pronunciation and raddoppiamento rules); entries for verbs (aìre, èssere, fare, dire, ulìre, putìre, sapìre, sçire, stare, enìre, tare, ìtere, tenìre); function words; interjections; proverbs and 'modi di dire'; vulgar entries (cazzu, mìnchia, fessa, culu, curnutu, futtìre, mannàggia, etc.)

sources.title: Vocabolario dei dialetti salentini (Terra d'Otranto), vol. III: Supplemento, Repertorio italiano-salentino, Indici
sources.author: Gerhard Rohlfs
sources.publisher: Bayerische Akademie der Wissenschaften (open PDF on tll-open.badw.de)
sources.license: Copyright 1961 Bayerische Akademie der Wissenschaften; made openly available online by the Academy
sources.reliability_notes: The standard reference work. Only volume III (the Italian-Salentino repertory) was available and was read through text extraction. Volumes I-II (the Salentine-Italian part, with locality labels) were not consulted, so Rohlfs is cited only for facts checked in vol. III: the forms listed under 'bestemmia', 'stupido', 'pene', 'nessuno', 'lavorare' and 'andare'. Its entries are pan-Salentine and often lack a locality, so Lecce forms were always confirmed in Garrisi.

sources.title: I dialetti perileccesi
sources.author: Antonio Romano
sources.publisher: In P. Pascali & D. Capone (eds.), L'ombra di Tancredi, Giorgiani (author's manuscript on AperTO, Università di Torino)
sources.linguistic_area: Dialects around Lecce (Cavallino, Lizzanello, Lequile, Monteroni, Vernole, Trepuzzi, Squinzano)
sources.license: Open access author's manuscript (rights with author/publisher)
sources.reliability_notes: Peer-level academic description. It lists the features shared around Lecce: cacuminal -ḍḍ-, Sicilian-type vowels with metaphonic diphthongs ie/ue, the 2pl clitic bbu, the 'Lecce-type' possessives, reduced use of the infinitive, the progressive order 'se sta' (rather than 'sta sse') and regular raddoppiamento fonosintattico. It also gives the full possessive set (miu/mia/mei; tou/toa/toi; sou/soa/soi; nuesciu/noscia/nuesci/nosce; uesciu/oscia/uesci/osce; loru).

sources.title: Siciliani, calabresi e salentini, dialetti (Enciclopedia dell'Italiano)
sources.author: Francesco Avolio
sources.reliability_notes: Scholarly encyclopedia article. Used for the five-vowel stressed system, the cacuminal outcome of -ll-, cacuminal tr/str, the wɛ diphthong (bbuenu vs bbona), voiceless stops kept after nasals, the 'ku' clause replacing the infinitive, the repeated imperfect in counterfactuals, crai 'tomorrow', and the spellings dd/ddh/ddr.

sources.title: Salentino dialect
sources.reliability_notes: Classification (Extreme Southern Italian, after Avolio 2012). It also gives a small sample of sentences, taken from Golovko & Panov (aggiu ffare, iddu ulia cu llu ddicu, ci tinia fame mangiava). The page carries 'more citations needed' tags.

sources.title: Dialetti salentini
sources.linguistic_area: Salento (provinces of Lecce, Brindisi, south-eastern Taranto)
sources.reliability_notes: Encyclopedic summary drawing on Rohlfs, Mancarella, Parlangeli, Morosi, Panareo and Ribezzo. Used for the three-way north/centre/south division, vowel systems, syntax ('ku'/'ka', the future and progressive periphrases, the imperfect-indicative hypothetical), the pronoun table, 'signurìa', and the proverbs and phrases it lists. Facts were rephrased.
sources.relevant_sections: Fonetica, Sintassi, Morfologia, Varianti, Dialetti salentini e dialetti pugliesi, Proverbi, Fraseologia

sources.title: Dialetto leccese
sources.reliability_notes: Used for the Lecce present/imperfect/perfect of essere, avere and scire, the progressive 'sta + finite verb', the future strategies, local differences (bu vs ve, li vs le, the Grecìa remote past, 'sta me uardi' vs 'me sta uardi') and a long list of common words.
sources.relevant_sections: Differenze dall'italiano standard, Altre differenze territoriali, Verbi, Parole di uso comune

sources.title: Dialetto salentino meridionale
sources.linguistic_area: Southern Salento (south of the Gallipoli-Maglie-Otranto line)
sources.reliability_notes: Used only for the contrasts with the southern variety: no conditioned diphthongs, affricated cacuminal (beddhru), unstressed vowels tending to a.

sources.title: Proverbi salentini
sources.reliability_notes: A short list of sourced proverbs (citing Romano, Malecore, Lezzi and local press). Spellings vary by locality, so only items consistent with Lecce forms were used.

sources.title: 30 modi di dire siciliani (quasi) intraducibili (Balarm)
sources.reliability_notes: Popular article (G. Caccialupi, 21 Apr 2024); spellings partly western.

sources.title: Dalla A di Annacati alla Z di Ziccusu: l'alfabeto della 'raggia' (Balarm)
sources.reliability_notes: Popular article (G. Tantillo, 9 Feb 2024); several forms are western (ri, giarnu) and are NOT used for Catanese.

sources.title: Sicily (report, PRIN 2017 'Models of language variation and change'; suppl. material to Guardiano, Cambria & Stalfieri 2022, Languages 7:255)
sources.reliability_notes: Academic report summarising Piccitto 1950, Ruffino 1997, Varvaro 1988. Used for isoglosses (Catanese-Syracusan assimilation of preconsonantal R; western palatalisation of preconsonantal r), preterite use for recent past, kinship possessives.
sources.relevant_sections: s.4 Consonants (isoglosses 14-23); s.5 morphology (no enclitic possessives, lack of analytic perfect: 'comu mangiasti'); s.6 nouns
sources.author: Vincenzo Stalfieri

sources.title: UD for Sicilian (Universal Dependencies documentation)
sources.reliability_notes: Treebank documentation; describes SVO with object fronting, pro-drop, clitic clusters, contractions, aviri a + infinitive, aviri as sole auxiliary, stari + gerund.
sources.relevant_sections: Word order; clitics (mû, tû, sû, mâ); contractions (â, dû, ô, ntô); aviri a; auxiliaries; progressive

sources.title: Sicilian language (English Wikipedia)
sources.reliability_notes: Well-referenced article (Bonner 2001, Camilleri 1998, Pitre, Cipolla, Ledgeway). Grammar describes the literary/koine norm, not Catanese specifically.
sources.relevant_sections: Dialects (Catanese = Eastern non-metaphonetic); Phonology; Gemination and contractions; Grammar (nouns, aviri, jiri a, essiri table, future/conditional replacements, imperative); Martoglio extract; sample phrases

sources.title: Italian profanity (English Wikipedia)
sources.reliability_notes: Notes minchia as Sicilian-origin; minchiata; testa di minchia.

sources.title: Proverbi siciliani (Wikiquote in italiano)
sources.linguistic_area: Sicilian (mostly pan-Sicilian, from Pitre, Scarcella, Traina and others)
sources.reliability_notes: Collection with references to 19th-century collections (Pitre 1880, Scarcella 1846, Traina 1868). Most proverbs are pan-Sicilian, a few show Catanese phonology (potta, cutta, voddiri, riscussu).
sources.relevant_sections: A-Z proverb list with Italian glosses

sources.title: Wiktionary, Sicilian entries (via kaikki.org machine-readable extraction)
sources.linguistic_area: Sicilian (all varieties; some entries labelled Catania)
sources.reliability_notes: Community dictionary; entries rarely give regional labels. Used for existence, meaning and register (vulgar/derogatory tags) of single words. Entry 'mbari read directly at https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%27mbari.
sources.relevant_sections: Entries: 'mbari, cumpari, cummari, minchia, minchiata, suca, sucari, spacchiu, spacchimi, pacchiu, sticchiu, buttana, cugghiuni, culu, va fa 'n culu, mmunnizza, malanova, babbu, sceccu, annunca, antura, tannu, mammurianu (Catania), purpu, jarrusu, etc.
